rooms.message: Walk north to the isolated wall and hold Up. Chip must face north, remain in place, and keep pushing until Up is released.
Walk across the dirt and gravel patches. Both admit Chip; gravel hallways also form the safe route between rooms.
Collect the red key west of the divider, then cross the red door. The door and exactly one red key must both be consumed.
This room verifies room-specific Hint text. The message appears only after Chip finishes entering the Hint tile and disappears after Chip finishes leaving it.
Approach the dirt block from the south and push it north once. Chip and the block must begin and finish one synchronized ordinary push.
Push north against the trapped dirt block. Neither actor may move; Chip must face north and keep the push pose while Up remains held.
Stand directly north of the dirt block and press Right+Down together. Chip moves east while the block beside him is slapped south.
Stand west of the dirt block and push it east into water. The block must disappear when entry finishes and the water must become dirt.
Use the one-cell lane and tap or hold Right across two floor cells. Each ordinary step starts immediately, is halfway one logic boundary later, and finishes two boundaries after it starts.
Push the dirt-block actor north through the one-cell choke while holding Up. The block commits first, vacates its old cell immediately, and Chip enters that same cell on the same boundary.
In the upper lane, push the dirt block west onto gravel and then walk across it. In the sealed lower lane, the pink ball repeatedly tries and fails to enter gravel.
Watch the pink ball reject the Exit at the east end of its sealed lane. Approach that same Exit from the north: only Chip may enter, and the win occurs when entry finishes.
Collect the red key, then enter the red door in the divider. The count goes from zero to one to zero; the door remains during entry and disappears when entry finishes.
Collect the blue key, then enter the blue door in the divider. The blue count goes from zero to one to zero, and every inventory sample must remain visibly blue.
Collect the yellow key, then enter the yellow door in the divider. The finite yellow key is consumed once and the completed entry removes the door.
Collect the green key and cross both green doors. DAT green-key possession is reusable: both doors open and the same green key remains possessed without displaying an infinity count.
Collect the red key below the divider. Try the blue door on the left, which must reject without spending it, then use the red door on the right, which consumes it.
Collect both red keys before crossing the two red-door dividers. The count must progress zero, one, two, one, zero, removing one door per completed entry.
Upper lane: push the dirt block east across the blue key. Sealed lower lane: a pink ball crosses another blue key. Each blue key is destroyed without creating inventory.

Each open row has a block immediately east of a red, green, or yellow key; push west. Each sealed row below has a pink ball facing the same color. Red admits nonplayers and remains; green and yellow reject them, then remain collectible by Chip.

The raw DAT header says one chip, but an ordered valid field-2 value says three and a later malformed one-byte field is ignored. Collect all three chips and open the socket using the imported requirement of three.
Collect the only two chips, then try the socket. Its threshold is three, so it rejects; inventory remains two and the backward-compatible UI reports one chip remaining.
Collect exactly three chips, then enter the socket. It opens only when entry finishes and does not spend any of the three gray chips.

Collect the three chips before the first divider and open both sockets in sequence. Each independently checks threshold three and spends nothing; leave the fourth chip beyond the second socket untouched.
Enter the socket without collecting any chips. A zero-threshold socket admits Chip and disappears only when entry finishes; inventory remains unchanged.
This is intentionally neutral support space. It carries no scenario ID; return to the gravel hallway and use the northwest room for the zero-socket check.
This is intentionally neutral support space. It carries no scenario ID; return to the gravel hallway and use the northwest room for the zero-socket check.
This is intentionally neutral support space. It carries no scenario ID; return to the gravel hallway and use the northwest room for the zero-socket check.
Collect the flippers and fire boots. Each pickup disappears only when entry finishes and appears in its named HUD slot.
Collect the ice skates and suction boots. Each pickup must appear in the correct named HUD slot.
Collect both copies of every boot. Hybrid keeps exact duplicate counts while the HUD still shows each named tool in its proper slot.
Collect all keys and tools, cross the first thief, then re-enter it empty: tools vanish but keys remain. Refill tools and enter the blue-door-over-thief cell; its blue key and tools clear together.
Fatal branch: enter the lone water tile without protection. Safe branch: collect flippers, cross the two-tile water strip, and return; the water remains.
Fatal branch: enter the lone fire tile unprotected. Safe branch: collect fire boots, cross the two-tile fire strip, and return; the fire remains.
Push the dirt block east into water. At completed entry the block disappears, the water becomes dirt, and one push plus water-fill consequence is reported.
Push the dirt block east onto fire. The block survives on the fire and the fire terrain does not change.
The sealed glider enters water, survives, and continues around its wall-bounded ring on later moves.
Eight sealed actors each have water as their only open destination. Ant, fireball, ball, tank, teeth, walker, blob, and centipede disappear on completed entry while Chip remains safe.
The sealed fireball enters fire, survives, and continues around its wall-bounded ring.
Eight sealed non-fireballs each face fire as their only open destination. Every attempt rejects before movement, so all actors and fire tiles remain.
Push the dirt block east onto its bomb. The sealed pink ball also enters a bomb autonomously. Each bomb and entering nonplayer disappear while the level continues.
Fatal branches: enter the west bomb for an ordinary bomb loss, or the east bomb-over-exit cell to prove loss dominates a simultaneous win proposal.
Fatal branches: enter the yellow-key-over-water cell, or enter the bomb-over-water cell. Layer consequences settle once; the later bomb proposal wins over water.
Press east into the wall shielding the tank; blocked terrain must prevent hostile contact. The sealed pink ball and fireball also reject each other without either disappearing.

The ball in the small enclosure intentionally presses the ordinary wall to its right; it causes no reveal. Below, Player can press the visible ordinary wall on the left or a hidden permanent wall on the right. Both block; only the hidden wall flashes.
The sealed monster rejects the invisible wall without revealing it. In the open fixture, a diagonal side attempt reveals the invisible wall while Chip's primary move still succeeds.

Player may enter the fake blue wall and turns it into floor; pressing the real one reveals an ordinary wall. Monster attempts reject without Player-only changes, even when one then takes a legal fallback.
Press into the invisible appearing wall twice. The first rejected attempt permanently changes it into an ordinary wall; the second sees that wall.
Codes 51-53 and 57-59 remain solid static art. Codes 54-56 become standard permanent invisible walls. Codes 60-63 remain solid directional swimming art. None creates a live actor.
Approach each cardinal panel from both sides and unrelated edges. Named edges block bidirectionally; the southeast corner blocks east and south only.
Bare pop-up rises after Chip leaves. The block-over-pop-up starts at count two: block departure leaves one recessed use so Chip may follow, then Chip departure raises it.
Push the block off the real blue wall: it leaves, the wall rises, and Chip must retry elsewhere. A bare pop-up admits Player but rejects a pushed dirt block and the sealed hostile.
Push the west block north, then the east block east. Each accepted push moves Chip and the block together, occupies both destinations immediately, and finishes after two boundaries.
Push the west block south, then approach the east block from its right and push west. These complete the four cardinal direct-push cases.
Hold into each wall-backed block from its open side. Chip must face and keep pushing in the attempted north, east, south, or west direction; neither actor moves.
Try the upper pair of adjacent blocks, then the lower block backed by a living pink ball. Classic Hybrid v1 has no push chain: both attempted transactions reject and every resident survives.
Stand north of the block and press East then South. East is Chip's primary move; South is the slap that moves the adjacent block.
Stand west of the block and press South then East. South is Chip's primary move; East is the slap. Input order, not compass sorting, selects the legs.
Use the four isolated fixtures to slap south, north, north, and south while Chip's legal primary move continues east, east, west, and west respectively.

Upper-left: a wall blocks only the slap. Upper-right: a wall blocks the East primary, then ordinary South fallback directly pushes the block with no slap probe. Lower-left: an invisible slap-side wall reveals while the primary succeeds.
Push the block north on ordinary floor. The block vacates its source first, then Chip follows into that source; both movements take two logic boundaries.
This DAT block starts over a real blue wall, converted to one recessed departure. The block leaves, the wall rises immediately, and Chip cannot follow it.
This DAT block starts over a pop-up wall, converted to count two. Block departure leaves count one, Chip follows, and Chip's later departure raises the wall.
The block's destination is a wall. A rejected push must not run the block source's StartExit hook, so its count-two pop-up source remains unchanged.
Push the west block north onto floor for a two-boundary interval. Push the east block north onto ice for an immediate one-boundary interval and an ice-owned continuation.
Push the west block north onto force for a one-boundary pushed interval; force then owns it. Push the east block north onto gravel for an ordinary two-boundary interval.

A block authored on ice is stationary and may be pushed sideways. A block authored on east force is terrain-owned but blocked by a wall; push it north, then immediately hold west or south so Chip leaves the blocked force floor.

The west loop drives a pushed block back into stationary Chip; only Chip dies at block StartMove. The east ice lane separates one player push interval from later ice-owned sliding for sound and pose checks.

Chip began on the ice at the room center. Construction did not give ice control: the first perpendicular input moved onto ordinary floor in two boundaries. Re-entering ice later does transfer control.
Nine sealed monster lanes begin on ice. Eight use ordinary AI to move onto floor; teeth turns toward Chip and rejects its sealed lane. None receives an automatic ice slide from construction.

The block began on ice but stays still. Approach from west and hold east. First push exposes ice and speeds Chip's entry. On the next boundary Chip catches the moving block, settles its old leg once, and immediately pushes again instead of bouncing.

Three fixtures enter ice from floor. Chip at the west fixture, the sealed pink ball above, and the pushable block below each commit the first ice-bound interval in one boundary; ownership transfers only at completion.
Collect the skates west of the ice strip. Every move onto, along, or sideways off ice remains a two-boundary player-input move; ice never takes control while skates are held.

Enter either straight strip without skates and release input. At every completion boundary ice immediately starts the next forward one-boundary leg. The sealed ball demonstrates the same ownership independently.

Enter a two-cell ice strip toward its wall. On the boundary the forward move fails, ice immediately reverses onto the preceding ice cell instead of idling. The sealed ball below repeats the same plan.

The ball leaves a solid real-blue source for ice. That source blocks reverse and the closed green toggle wall blocks forward, so ice keeps ownership and retries. Step on the green button to open its forward side.
Approach each upper corner from the north. The northeast corner turns east and the northwest corner turns west, each onto its other open edge without an idle boundary.

Four sealed balls enter the four corner orientations. Each redirected opening is walled, so ice rejects that preferred exit and immediately returns through the clear arrival edge; it never chooses a solid corner edge.
Approach each lower corner from the south. The southeast corner turns east and the southwest corner turns west, each onto its other open edge without an idle boundary.
The sealed ball moves south from a solid real-blue source into a northeast corner. Its east opening and its north source are blocked, so it remains corner-owned and retries only those two open edges.

Enter the eight-cell ice strip from the west. Arrival and ice-to-ice legs are N+1. The final ice-owned move lands on floor, so it is N+2; it starts at the prior completion and slows smoothly without a pause.

Hold Right through the seven-cell ice strip. Its final floor-bound move is N+2, begins without an idle boundary, and slows smoothly. The next held floor move starts exactly at completion and is also N+2.

Push the block east onto six ice cells. The fast entry has one player-push cause. Later ice-owned legs stay fast only when landing on ice; they remain collision-capable but emit no new push event or pose.

Teeth and blob move fast while landing on ice; their final floor-bound leg is N+2, then every-fourth cadence resumes. The lower tank keeps sliding; a blue-button edge during ice ownership does not reverse it.
Chip starts on east force. At boundary one the open east arrow owns the move, and conflicting input cannot override it. Its ordinary-floor destination makes the move N+2.
Nine sealed hostiles start on east force. Terrain owns each first move, even for teeth and blob; ordinary AI and cooldown do not choose it. The floor-bound moves are N+2.
The west block starts on open east force and moves immediately to floor at N+2. The east block's arrow is walled; a later north push supersedes force only for that N+2 floor-bound push.
West: Chip enters force fast, then leaves to floor at N+2. North: a ball does the same. South: collect suction boots and cross directional and random force as ordinary terrain.
Enter the east arrow from the west, then hold north, south, or west in separate branches. Its open east move always wins; the floor-bound automatic leg is N+2.
Top-left: blocked east allows north/south override. Top-right: blocked east allows west. All land on floor and take N+2. Bottom: automatic east legally pushes the block and wins before input.
Enter east force holding blocked north. Arrival consumes that failed offer. Later change to open south: the override starts immediately but is N+2 because it lands on floor.
Chip starts on east force with east blocked and north open. Boundary one records only blocked terrain control. North is eligible next boundary and takes N+2 to floor.
Blocked east arrows allow overrides onto floor, ice, force, and teleport. Ice/force landings are N+1; floor/teleport are N+2. Override chooses direction, destination chooses duration.
Nine sealed hostiles start on east force with east blocked and other space available. They stay force-owned and never borrow Chip's sideways/backward fallback.
Enter north holding south. Arrival and internal overrides land on force at N+1 with no idle or jolt. The final floor-bound move starts immediately but is N+2.
Enter the blocked east arrow from north holding south. The floor-bound override starts immediately but is N+2. The next held floor move starts on its exact completion, with no idle sample.
Enter the three random pads in separate seeded branches. Each decision draws a full permutation, selects its first legal direction, and takes N+2 when that direction lands on floor.
Enter random force holding another legal direction. The seeded permutation chooses north first; that automatic move legally pushes the block and wins. Both floor-bound legs are N+2.
Leave the count-one pop-up west of random force so it rises behind Chip. Ordinary walls then block every direction; each force opportunity consumes four draws, remains blocked, and retains ownership.

Three tracks compare open force arrows. Ice-to-force cannot preempt the arrow. A force-owned move through ice may preempt the next arrow once; a Player override through ice may not. Middle and lower fixtures retain boot and destination tests.

The ball crosses local green buttons at boundaries 3 and 7, then is destroyed. The initially closed and open walls each change on both edges, proving both complete parity cycles without later stray presses.
Support room: the paired open and closed toggle-wall proof is in the northwest room, where one finite ball track supplies exactly two local edges.
After the two-edge ball cycle, an ant reaches the upper green button at boundary 9 and a tank reaches the lower one at 11. Every mixed-polarity wall follows both global edges.

This actor matrix presses green with ball and ant together at 15, tank at 19, pushed block at 21, and Chip at 23. Hold east at 19, then north at 21; exact actor-bound event proofs distinguish the simultaneous pair.
The upper pair reaches green together at boundary 3 in left-then-right order. The lower pair reaches green at 5 with the opposite declared order. Each two-edge batch preserves wall parity.
After the four-edge parity batches, the long-run ball supplies edge five at boundary 9. The toggle closes beneath the east-facing tank while its gate opens, so the tank departs without being erased.
Hold east once to show Chip blocked at the first closed toggle. Walk south to the block lane and try east again before boundary 9; a ball independently bounces from another closed toggle.

The native snapshot publishes these walls unchanged after each even pair, then inverted on edge five at boundary 9. The local tank is blocked while closed and enters on that edge; the web host separately checks its 20 Hz art.
Four boxed tanks begin facing north, east, south, and west. The monster blue edge at boundary 2 reverses all four; the block blue edge at 9 restores every original facing.
The east-facing tank starts an ordinary move at boundary 1. Blue arrives at 2 while it is still in flight; on completion at 3 its next eligible move immediately uses west.
The blue edge at boundary 2 arrives during fast terrain-owned travel. Both tanks continue east on boundary 3; the signal neither reverses them immediately nor queues a later reversal.

Hold east: block presses green/red/brown/blue at 3/5/7/9 and Chip follows at 5/7/9/11. The balls cover all four colors; bomb-on-brown releases atomically at 3. The host maps interaction facts to audio.
The ball was authored on an unlinked DAT trap. Across multiple logic boundaries it remains the same actor in the same cell, with the holding trap retaining movement ownership.
Chip faces west in the linked trap. East input wins on release; blocked north input visibly reveals a wall before west facing succeeds.
The separately listed Blocked Retry variant isolates the later-opening-exit proof so this Player fixture stays unambiguous.
Support room reserved for walking and visual comparison without another linked component changing the Player proof.
Chip first retries against four blocked exits. Green later opens east while brown remains held, and fresh east input starts the departure immediately.

The east-facing ant has east and north open. Trap release chooses east facing before the ant's ordinary left-turn policy.
This east-facing ant has an east wall. Release rejects facing, then accepts its north AI fallback on the same boundary.
Teeth and blob move east into holding traps at boundary one. Brown releases at completion, but blocked facing cannot fall back until T+4.
A second teeth/blob pair proves the same release remains live through cooldown and launches only on its boundary-five opportunity.
The west trap is truly unlinked. At boundary three a separate local brown component releases its east trap while the unlinked occupant stays owned.
Alpha presses at boundary three and releases two traps while beta stays held. Beta presses at boundary five, proving independent components and one-button fanout.
One occupied blocked trap and one empty trap change from holding to releasing on the exact brown completion. This certifies semantics, not pixels.
Dedicated logical variants isolate Player, block, and monster handoffs plus rehold and reopen races without simultaneous-room cross-talk.
Chip presses brown first, the ball presses its separate brown button, and Chip later pushes the block onto a third. Each edge has its own trapped witness.

The common red component launches four directional blocks and nine classic mobs into separate lanes, preserving kind and facing. Chip's cloner consumes the same edge without cloning Player.
Walk onto red. Its edge appears only when Chip finishes entering; the block source then launches and is replenished.
A monster and a pushed dirt block use separate red components. Each completed entry emits its own edge and launches only its linked source.
Red first finds a shut toggle wall and spends its edge. Green opens the wall without retrying; the next red entry launches the still-waiting source.
Try Chip, a pushed block, and a monster against occupied cloner sources. Every approach rejects without displacing either source.
A slow block launch vacates the source logically at StartMove while presentation keeps a stationary source duplicate until FinishExit creates the real clone.
The west source launches to ordinary floor in N+2; the east source launches onto ice in N+1, then ice takes ownership after completion.
A source launches onto force in N+1. At completion the source clone appears exactly once and force becomes movement owner for the launched actor.
A cloner launches onto teleport using destination timing. Only after FinishEnter does teleport own and search its network; cloning and teleporting never collapse into one instant action.
Enter red from below and keep holding north. Chip is earlier than the east-facing source, but the fresh dependent input waits; the block claims the north cell and Chip rejects alive.
Approach this red button from below and keep holding north. The source is earlier than Chip and claims the north cell before Chip's fresh attempt, again rejecting without death.
Red releases two cloners while brown releases two trapped balls. Both pairs target one empty square; reversed DAT order makes a different actor win each twin.
A ball finishes red while Chip continues across unrelated open floor. The later cloner and Chip both start their independent moves on that boundary.
A block launch fills water and dies while its source is replenished. Fireball admits to fire and survives; ant rejects fire admission and stays at source.
A launched actor completes onto a bomb; both are destroyed while the source clone appears exactly once and future red edges remain usable.
Independent red buttons launch a block or hostile into Chip. Accepted StartMove destroys only Chip; the launched actor and source-clone lifecycle continue after loss.

A cloner-owned tank ignores the early blue reversal edge. One red component then fans out twice to tank and teeth; a staggered independent component clones ant twice without cross-talk, preserving each source's actual facing.
